sentences.text: The marriage between petitioner no.2/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 23.11.2019 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
9. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 2 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 12.10.2020.
Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against petitioner no.1 (mother-in-law), petitioner no. 2 (husband) and petitioner no. 3 (brother-in-law) and petitioner no. 4 (father-in-law).

10. On 10.12.2021, parties arrived at a settlement before Counseling Cell, Family Courts and as per the said settlement deed, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 6,00,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan,
permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.

The copy of the aforesaid settlement dated 10.12.2021 is on record (Annexure P-3).
11.

sentences.text: Further, as per the settlement deed, an amount of Rs. 4,00,000/- has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- has been paid to her in court today, by means of a demand draft.

12. Petitioners no. 1, 2 and 4, and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, S.I. Ekta,
P.S: Dabri.
13.

sentences.text: A demand draft bearing no. 462061, dated 27.03.2023, for Rs. 2,00,000/- drawn on State Bank of India has been handed over complainant/Respondent No.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.
15. The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.
16. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 996/2021, under Section 498A/406/34/354B of the IPC, registered at P.S.
